summary: Rejected the AI-native-drug-discovery relationship to NVIDIA at low sensitivity and low confidence. The Lilly co-innovation lab establishes a concrete compute, software and laboratory-integration channel, but the up-to-USD-1-billion five-year commitment is not NVIDIA revenue and does not establish material, repeatable life-sciences economics relative to NVIDIA's diversified Data Center business. Measurable multi-customer revenue or software economics are the upgrade gate; no strategy or follow-up operation was created.

evidence.claim: Lilly describes up to USD 1 billion over five years for a co-innovation lab using NVIDIA infrastructure and software, but does not allocate that commitment to NVIDIA revenue or profit.
The maintained idea confirms tool adoption but not generalized clinical success and identifies pharma internalization as a risk to supplier economics.
NVIDIA's maintained review reports USD 75.246 billion of quarterly Data Center revenue and no comparable life-sciences economic line.

daily_report_items: Rejected NVIDIA as a current AI-drug-discovery investment edge: a concrete Lilly lab supports relevance but not material, recurring shareholder economics.
